outline: 1942 Permutations involving Grouping, Complements, and Cases

examples.question_text: A club has $13$ members. In how many ways can a president, secretary and treasurer be appointed if each member holds at most one role?
examples.solution_text:
The roles are distinct. There are $13$ choices for president, $12$ for secretary and $11$ for treasurer.

$\begin{aligned} N&={}^{13}P_{3}\\&=13\times12\times11\\&=1716 \end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Find the positive integer $n$ such that $^{n}P_{2}=90$.

examples.solution_text:
Try descending products starting from $10$:

$\begin{aligned} {}^{10}P_{1}&=10\\{}^{10}P_{2}&=10\times9=90\\{}^{10}P_{3}&=10\times9\times8=720 \end{aligned}$

The product uses three factors, so $r=3$.

The permutations require $n\ge2$.

$\begin{aligned} (n+1)n(n-1)&=30(n-1) \end{aligned}$

Divide both sides by $n-1$, which is non-zero.

$\begin{aligned} n(n+1)&=30\\n^{2}+n-30&=0\\(n+6)(n-5)&=0 \end{aligned}$

Since $n\ge2$, $n=5$.

examples.derivation: Three distinct roles without repetition give 13 × 12 × 11 = 1716 appointments.
n(n−1) = 90 gives (n−10)(n+9) = 0. The admissible positive integer is n = 10.
8 × 7 × 6 = 336; 9 × 8 × 7 = 504. Descending three-factor products increase for integer n ≥ 3, so n = 9 uniquely.
Starting from 10, the products are 10, 90 and 720. Three factors give r = 3; subsequent products exceed 720.
The domain requires n ≥ 2. Cancelling n−1 yields n(n+1) = 30, hence (n+6)(n−5) = 0. Only n = 5 is admissible; substitution gives 6P3 = 120 = 30 × 4P1.
With common denominator (n−r+1)!, the RHS numerator is [(n−r+1)+r]n! = (n+1)!. Thus the RHS equals (n+1)!/(n+1−r)! = (n+1)Pr throughout the stated domain.
